_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Namibia covering San rock art (Twyfelfontein), Bantu migration, Herero/Nama peoples, German South-West Africa, Herero/Nama genocide (1904–1908, first genocide of the 20th century), South African mandate, SWAPO liberation struggle, independence 1990 (last African colony), and Skeleton Coast.

ethnic_groups.name: Ovambo (Aawambo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; northern Namibia; Ovamboland; Oshiwambo-speaking; 8 sub-groups including Kwanyama, Ndonga, Kwambi; SWAPO political base

ethnic_groups.name: Kavango
ethnic_groups.notes: Northeastern Namibia; Okavango River; five ethnic groups: Kwangali, Mbunza, Sambyu, Gciriku, Mbukushu

ethnic_groups.name: Damara
ethnic_groups.notes: Ancient Khoisan-speaking people; historically displaced by Nama and Herero; Khoekhoegowab language

ethnic_groups.name: Herero
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu pastoralists; central Namibia; 1904–1908 genocide victims (80% killed); Victorian dress legacy; Omaheke; related groups: Himba, Mbanderu

ethnic_groups.name: White Namibians
ethnic_groups.notes: Afrikaner, German, Portuguese, British; commercial farming; Afrikaans/German/English-speaking

ethnic_groups.name: Nama
ethnic_groups.notes: Khoekhoe people; southern Namibia; Khoekhoegowab; 1904–1908 genocide; distinct from Damara despite shared language

ethnic_groups.name: Coloured
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed-race; Rehoboth Basters semi-autonomous community; Afrikaans-speaking

ethnic_groups.name: Caprivian (Lozi/Masubia)
ethnic_groups.notes: Zambezi Region (Caprivi Strip); Lozi and related peoples; cross-border with Zambia; distinct from rest of Namibia; secessionist tensions

ethnic_groups.name: San/Bushmen
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous hunter-gatherers; oldest inhabitants; marginalized; !Kung, Ju/'hoansi, Hai//om groups; click languages

ethnic_groups.name: Himba
ethnic_groups.notes: Remote northwestern Namibia; Kunene; Herero-related pastoralists; distinctive ochre body decoration; traditional lifestyle preserved

independence.notes: Last African country to gain independence

country_profile.notes_unique: The Namib Desert is considered the world's oldest desert (55–80 million years); one of the least densely populated countries on Earth; Namibia's constitution was the first in Africa to include environmental protection.

natural_resources.notes: World's 4th-largest uranium producer (Rössing and Husab mines); De Beers joint venture Namdeb leading diamond producer; Namibia's constitution (Article 95) was first in Africa to mandate environmental protection; Green Hydrogen project (Hyphen) planned; rich marine fisheries (Benguela current); SACU member.

military.notes: Namibia Defence Force (NDF); formed from PLAN (SWAPO guerrilla force) and SWATF after independence; deployed in DR Congo (SADC); professional reputation; limited naval capacity despite long Atlantic coast.

infrastructure.notes: MTC, Telecom Namibia; well-maintained road network; TransNamib rail; Walvis Bay hub.

debt_aid.notes: Upper-middle-income economy; SACU revenues important (~30% of government revenue); high inequality (Gini ~59, one of world's highest); Green Hydrogen project ($10B+) could transform economy; Fishrot corruption scandal.

top_universities: Namibia University of Science and Technology (NUST)
education.notes: Free primary education; high literacy rate; English is language of instruction (despite being L3 for most); SACMEQ assessments; teacher quality challenges in rural communal conservancies; strong environmental education tradition.

diaspora_migration.notes: German-speaking Namibian community maintains ties to Germany; skilled professionals emigrate to South Africa; Angolan refugees in north; SWAPO exile community largely returned post-1990.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Hosts Angolan refugees; SADC free movement

digital_economy.notes: WACS submarine cable; MTC and Telecom Namibia operators; growing fintech sector; NCRST (commission for research) supports innovation; relatively high mobile penetration; rural connectivity challenge.

geography.terrain: Namib Desert (west, oldest desert); Kalahari Desert (east); Central Plateau; Caprivi Strip (northeast panhandle); Skeleton Coast; Fish River Canyon
geography.notes: 2nd least densely populated country globally; Namib Desert (~55 million years old, oldest); Skeleton Coast; Fish River Canyon (2nd largest); Caprivi Strip; Etosha NP.

economy_extended.notes: Mining dependent (diamonds—De Beers Namdeb, uranium—Rössing/Husab, zinc); fishing (hake); beef exports; highest inequality (Gini 59.1); hydrogen hub ambitions (green H2 pilot with Germany).

health.notes: High HIV prevalence but strong ART programme (90-90-90 target); TB one of highest globally; health tourism from Angola; Windhoek Central Hospital.

food_agriculture.notes: Arid climate limits agriculture; livestock farming (beef exports to EU); fishing industry (hake, horse mackerel); grape/wine production (Orange River); water scarcity.

energy.notes: Imports 60% electricity from South Africa and Zambia; Ruacana hydro dam; green hydrogen Hyphen project (planned $10B); massive solar potential; NamPower utility.

transport.notes: TransNamib railway; well-maintained tar road network; Walvis Bay container terminal; B1/B2 highways (Trans-Caprivi); no national airline since 2021.

tourism.notes: Adventure and wildlife tourism; Sossusvlei/Deadvlei iconic landscapes; Etosha world-class safari; German colonial heritage; eco-tourism leader; community conservancies.

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Legal (decriminalized 2024 – Supreme Court struck down sodomy law)
human_rights_gender.notes: One of Africa's most stable democracies; SWAPO dominance since independence; land reform ongoing (German genocide reparations); high women in parliament.

border_disputes: Kasikili/Sedudu Island (settled by ICJ 1999 in favor of Botswana)
security_stability.notes: Peaceful and stable; independence from South Africa 1990; German genocide of Herero and Nama (1904-08) — Germany recognized 2021; low crime.

national_symbols: welwitschia plant (national emblem on coat of arms)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: NBC state broadcaster; The Namibian (independent, critical); diverse private media; press freedom strong
cultural_heritage.notes: German colonial heritage (architecture, language remnants, Oktoberfest); Herero genocide; San Bushmen culture; Welwitschia plant (1000+ years); community conservancy model (CBNRM).

legal_system.legal_tradition: Roman-Dutch law (South African heritage) and customary law
legal_system.customary_law_role: Traditional courts (community courts) handle local disputes
legal_system.notes: Strong constitution (progressive, post-apartheid model); Supreme Court independent; Roman-Dutch law basis; Ombudsman institution.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Among Africa's most free, peaceful, and well-governed nations.

current_leader.name: Nangolo Mbumba
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Acting President following Geingob's death; SWAPO; former VP

president_elect.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
president_elect.title: President-elect
president_elect.notes: SWAPO; first female president of Namibia; won November 2024 election; takes office March 2025; veteran SWAPO leader

former_leaders.name: Sam Nujoma
former_leaders.notes: Founding president; SWAPO leader since 1960; father of the nation; three terms; retired voluntarily

former_leaders.name: Hifikepunye Pohamba
former_leaders.notes: SWAPO; Mo Ibrahim Prize 2014 for good governance; voluntarily stepped down

former_leaders.name: Hage Geingob
former_leaders.notes: SWAPO; first PM 1990–2002; died in office February 2024 from cancer

910.name: San Rock Art and Early Inhabitants
910.description: San hunter-gatherers inhabit Namibia for tens of thousands of years; Twyfelfontein rock engravings are a UNESCO World Heritage site; Damara and Nama Khoikhoi peoples also ancient inhabitants.

sub_clusters.name: Twyfelfontein Rock Engravings
sub_clusters.description: UNESCO World Heritage site in Kunene region with over 2,500 rock engravings and paintings; depict animals, human footprints, and geometric designs; created by San hunter-gatherers.

sub_clusters.name: San and Damara Ancient Populations
sub_clusters.description: San (Bushmen) hunter-gatherers are the earliest inhabitants; Damara people (Khoikhoi linguistic group) establish pastoral communities; diverse ecological adaptations across desert, savanna, and coastal environments.

920.name: Bantu Migration and Pastoral Peoples
920.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate into northern and central Namibia; Herero pastoralists and Ovambo agro-pastoralists establish distinct societies.

sub_clusters.name: Ovambo Settlement in Northern Namibia
sub_clusters.description: Ovambo-speaking peoples settle in the well-watered Cuvelai drainage system (Owamboland); develop mixed farming economy; become the largest ethnic group in Namibia.

sub_clusters.name: Herero Migration into Central Namibia
sub_clusters.description: Herero pastoralists migrate from East Africa via the Kaokoveld into central Namibia; cattle-centred culture; holy fire (okuruwo) ritual traditions; competition with Nama for grazing.

930.name: Nama-Herero Conflicts and European Contact
930.description: Nama-Herero wars over cattle and grazing; Oorlam groups introduce firearms; European missionaries and traders arrive; Jonker Afrikaner's dominance.

sub_clusters.name: Nama-Herero Wars and Oorlam Impact
sub_clusters.description: Nama clans clash with Herero over central highlands grazing; Oorlam Afrikaners (Jonker Afrikaner) dominate from Windhoek with firearms and horse tactics.

sub_clusters.name: Maharero's Herero Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Maharero unites Herero groups; negotiates with German traders and missionaries; Battle of Otjimbingwe 1880; fragile peace between Herero and Nama before German colonisation.

sub_clusters.name: Skeleton Coast and European Maritime Contact
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese navigator Diogo Cão reaches Cape Cross 1486; treacherous Skeleton Coast (shipwrecks, fog, desert); whaling and guano stations; Walvis Bay claimed by Britain 1878.

940.name: German South-West Africa
940.description: Germany colonises Namibia as South-West Africa; land confiscation and cattle seizure provoke the Herero and Nama uprisings; the resulting genocide is the first of the 20th century.

sub_clusters.name: German Colonisation and Land Seizure
sub_clusters.description: Heinrich Göring (father of Hermann) as imperial commissioner; Schutztruppe garrisons; treaties of protection then systematic land and cattle confiscation from Herero and Nama peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Herero and Nama Genocide (1904–1908)
sub_clusters.description: Herero revolt January 1904 under Samuel Maharero; Battle of Waterberg August 1904; General Lothar von Trotha's extermination order (Vernichtungsbefehl); Herero driven into Omaheke Desert; Nama uprising under Hendrik Witbooi; concentration camps (Shark Island); ~65,000 Herero (80%) and ~10,000 Nama (50%) killed. Recognised as the first genocide of the 20th century.

sub_clusters.name: German South-West Africa: Final Years
sub_clusters.description: Diamond rush at Lüderitz 1908; settler colonialism intensifies; World War I — South African forces invade and Germany surrenders South-West Africa in 1915.

940.name: South African Mandate and Apartheid Rule
940.description: South Africa administers Namibia under League of Nations mandate; extends apartheid system; reserves (bantustans) created; resistance grows.

sub_clusters.name: League of Nations Mandate
sub_clusters.description: South Africa receives Class C mandate; treats territory as de facto fifth province; white settlement encouraged; contract labour system for Ovambo workers.

sub_clusters.name: Apartheid Extended to Namibia
sub_clusters.description: South Africa extends apartheid laws; Odendaal Commission (1964) creates bantustans; forced removals; pass laws; Old Location shooting in Windhoek 1959.

950.name: SWAPO Liberation Struggle
950.description: SWAPO leads armed liberation struggle against South African occupation; international legal battles at ICJ; UN recognises Namibian independence right; Border War/Bush War.

sub_clusters.name: SWAPO Formation and Early Resistance
sub_clusters.description: South West Africa People's Organisation (SWAPO) founded 1960 by Sam Nujoma and others; ICJ rules on South Africa's obligations; UN revokes mandate 1966.

sub_clusters.name: Armed Struggle and Border War
sub_clusters.description: PLAN (People's Liberation Army of Namibia) launches armed struggle at Omgulumbashe 26 August 1966; South African Border War/Bush War; Angolan theatre; Cassinga massacre 1978.

sub_clusters.name: UN Resolution 435 and Independence Process
sub_clusters.description: UN Security Council Resolution 435 (1978) mandates supervised elections; linked to Cuban troop withdrawal from Angola; Battle of Cuito Cuanavale 1988 breaks stalemate; elections November 1989; independence 21 March 1990.

960.name: Independent Namibia
960.description: Namibia becomes the last African colony to gain independence; SWAPO dominates politics; reconciliation policy; land reform debates; Germany acknowledges genocide.

sub_clusters.name: Sam Nujoma's Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Nujoma serves three terms; policy of national reconciliation; progressive constitution; Caprivi secessionist attempt 1999; land redistribution begins slowly.

sub_clusters.name: Pohamba and Geingob Presidencies
sub_clusters.description: Hifikepunye Pohamba (2005–2015) wins Mo Ibrahim Prize; Hage Geingob (2015–2024) faces corruption allegations; SWAPO dominance slowly erodes; youth unemployment crisis.

sub_clusters.name: German Genocide Recognition
sub_clusters.description: Germany formally acknowledges Herero and Nama genocide in 2021; €1.1 billion development aid offer; Herero and Nama representatives reject terms as inadequate; reparations debate continues.

sub_clusters.name: Land Reform and Economic Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Willing-seller-willing-buyer land reform; white farmers still own disproportionate land; uranium and diamond mining; conservation economy (communal conservancies); Nana Mbumba becomes first female president 2024.
